long-spoons: The same table. The same food. The same long spoons.
The only difference was how they treated each other.
ant-grasshopper: All summer long, an ant carried food to its home,
The grasshopper was cold and hungry, with nothing at all.
tortoise-hare: The hare shot ahead and soon couldn't even see the tortoise.
So confident, he lay down under a tree for a nap.
Slowly. Step by step. Never stopping.
The tortoise had already crossed the finish line.
cookie-thief: A woman waiting for her flight bought a pack of cookies and sat down.
Every time she took one, so did he.
And there was her pack of cookies. Unopened.
She had been eating his cookies the whole time.
bear-friend: He lay on the ground and held his breath, pretending to be dead.
"He said, never trust a friend who leaves you in danger."
miser-gold: A rich miser sold everything he owned and bought a lump of gold.
and went every single day just to look at it.
The next morning, the miser screamed and cried.
His neighbour asked, "Did you ever use that gold?"
"Then bury a stone in that hole and look at it instead.
cried-wolf: A few days later, he did it again. "Wolf!"
Then one evening, a real wolf came.
Trust takes years to build and seconds to break.
thirsty-crow: On a hot summer day, a thirsty crow searched everywhere for water.
It tried to push the pitcher over. Too heavy.
But the crow looked around and saw small pebbles.
Slowly, the water rose. Higher and higher.
Until finally, the crow could drink.
empty-pot: He gave every child in the kingdom one seed.
"Whoever grows the most beautiful flower will be the next emperor."
When the day came, all the other children carried beautiful flowers.
Ping carried an empty pot. He was ashamed.
sour-grapes: A hungry fox saw a bunch of juicy grapes hanging high on a vine.
He jumped again, higher this time. Still nothing.
Again and again he tried, until he was exhausted.
But that lie keeps us from trying again.
